audience: Codex app-server, MCP, and multi-agent operators
candidate_text: Codex app-server MCP startup notifications now carry nullable `threadId`, so subagent MCP failures stay scoped to the owning thread instead of polluting the parent transcript. App-server clients should handle the new field. PR: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/26639
evidence_notes: The app-server protocol struct, JSON schema, and TypeScript type add nullable `threadId` to MCP startup notifications.
The app-server README documents `threadId` as the owning thread or null for app-scoped startup.
The TUI routes MCP startup notifications by thread and treats missing thread ids as app-scoped.
PR #26639 says child-owned MCP failures should not pollute the parent transcript.

claims.text: MCP startup notifications now include nullable thread ownership in the app-server protocol.
Subagent MCP startup failures should stay visible in the owning thread instead of the parent transcript.

decision.reason: The PR combines a concrete app-server protocol change with a visible multi-agent MCP diagnostic fix.

caveats: Clients with strict generated schemas may need to accept the new nullable field.
The TUI currently ignores app-scoped null notifications until an app-level target exists.
next_steps: Let Publisher automation decide whether to reserve or post this after repository checks pass.
